reference.title: Dumbbell Alternate Shoulder Press (male)
reference.listing: Video; data sheet: body part Shoulders, equipment Dumbbell, exercise type Strength
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe out on each press, breathe in as that arm lowers.
breathing.cadence: About 1.5 s up, short pause, about 1.8 s down per arm

prescription.load: User-chosen dumbbells; the EMG studies used 80% of 1RM (Saeterbakken 2012)
prescription.progression: Add reps, then weight; standing alternating press

cues.text: Back pad nearly upright, back on the pad, feet flat. Both dumbbells at shoulder height, palms forward, elbows under the wrists.
Breathe out and press the right dumbbell up while the left stays at the shoulder.
Right arm nearly straight overhead; trunk does not tilt.
Lower the right dumbbell in about 2 s back to shoulder height.
Now press the left dumbbell while the right holds at the shoulder.
Lower the left dumbbell under control; keep alternating.

mistakes.fix: Keep the back on the pad and the shoulders level.
Keep the waiting dumbbell at shoulder height, elbow under the wrist.

mistakes.mistake: Arching the low back off the pad

kinematics.norm: Seated presses are usually done with the back pad at 80-90 degrees (clinical opinion)
Pressing arm from about 80-90 degrees to about 160-170 degrees overhead (clinical opinion)
About 90 degrees at the bottom, nearly straight at the top (clinical opinion)
Holds the dumbbell at shoulder height (isometric); unilateral loading raises oblique and abdominal activity when seated (Saeterbakken 2012)
Controlled, one arm at a time (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #397212, Dumbbell Alternate Shoulder Press (male), video (movement reference)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2012, muscle activity of the core during bilateral, unilateral, seated and standing resistance exercise (Eur J Appl Physiol 112:1671-1678)
Campos et al. 2020, different shoulder exercises affect the activation of deltoid portions in resistance-trained individuals (J Hum Kinet 75:5-14)
Saeterbakken & Fimland 2013, effects of body position and loading modality on muscle activity and strength in shoulder presses (J Strength Cond Res 27(7):1824-1831)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Kick the dumbbells up from the thighs one at a time to start, and lower them back to the thighs at the end of the set.
modify: Shoulder pain overhead: press with palms facing in and the elbows further forward.
Low-back discomfort: keep the pad upright and the back against it.
regressions: Seated single-arm press with the free hand on the thigh.
progressions: Seated bilateral press with heavier loads.

muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_r: Main mover of the pressing arm; the other arm holds the dumbbell at the shoulder (isometric). Pressing gave the highest anterior deltoid activity of four exercises (Campos 2020).
muscleNotes.ant_deltoid_l: Main mover of the pressing arm; the other arm holds the dumbbell at the shoulder (isometric). Pressing gave the highest anterior deltoid activity of four exercises (Campos 2020).
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_r: Lifts the pressing arm up and out (Campos 2020); stays working in the holding arm.
muscleNotes.lat_deltoid_l: Lifts the pressing arm up and out (Campos 2020); stays working in the holding arm.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_r: Upward rotation and elevation of the shoulder blade overhead.
muscleNotes.upper_traps_l: Upward rotation and elevation of the shoulder blade overhead.
muscleNotes.serratus_r: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade.
muscleNotes.serratus_l: Upward rotation of the shoulder blade.
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Steadies the shoulders; lower seated than standing (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_l: Steadies the shoulders; lower seated than standing (Saeterbakken 2013).
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Rotator cuff: centres the ball of the shoulder.
muscleNotes.infraspinatus_l: Rotator cuff: centres the ball of the shoulder.
muscleNotes.obliques_r: Resist the side-to-side load: seated unilateral presses gave far more external oblique activity than seated bilateral (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.obliques_l: Resist the side-to-side load: seated unilateral presses gave far more external oblique activity than seated bilateral (Saeterbakken 2012).
muscleNotes.core: Holds the trunk against the pad; seated unilateral presses raised rectus abdominis activity over bilateral (Saeterbakken 2012).
